newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares rise to new high, helped by drugs.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares rise to new high, helped by drugs.

text.p: Swedish shares ended at another a new high for a second consecutive day on Tuesday, boosted by Wall Street's surge on reopening in afternoon trade and gains by forestry and drug shares.
The Stockholm general index rose 0.38 percent to 2,943.82 in turnover totalling 4.35 billion crowns

Drug company Astra rose 1.5 crowns to 141. After the market closed the company announced it had received FDA approval in the U.S. for its anti-asthma treatment Pulmicort Turbuhaler. The drug sector index rose 0.98 percent.
Keen buying interest from UBS lifted the Astra share. The bank has bought some six million shares in the drug company in the past week since placing a buy recommendation on it.

The forestry index rose 1.39 percent. Stora rose three crowns to 129 on a rumour that Finland's UPM Kymmene will buy all or parts of it. Fuelling this rumour was more talk that the Finnish company had tried to sell its stake in Nokia.
Nordbanken rose three crowns to 241 in heavy turnover. S-E-Banken edged up half a crown to 83.
"I wouldn't be surprised it someone was buying shares on pure speculation that something is going to happen," a broker said. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1003
